items.summary:
Fable 5.2가 세계 최고 모델이라지만, 새로워진 점을 느끼지 못해 지쳤다는 반응

Fable 5.2가 세계 최고 모델이라는데 아무 느낌이 없음
완전히 질렸음

Fable 5.2는 어제 나왔지만, 슈팅 게임 테스트도 돌려보지 않았음

7월 이후 새 모델은 프롬프트 하나만으로 3D 슈팅 게임을 만들어 왔음
Kimi 3, Fable 5, GPT-6 Astra, Opus 5.5가 그랬음
9월에는 Opus 5.5가 Blender 장면을 만들었고, 글쓴이는 이게 AGI냐고 소리 내어 물을 만큼 크게 놀랐음

이제는 엔터를 누르기 전부터 결과를 알고 있음
괜찮은 슈팅 게임이 나오겠지만, 이미 그런 게임은 충분히 있음

FrontierCode 2.0에서 Fable 5.2는 49.1%, Opus 5.5는 45.5%를 기록함
그래서 뭐가 달라지는지, 누가 신경 쓰는지 모르겠음

요즘 큰 데모는 에이전트 1,000개 이상과 컴퓨팅 8일 이상을 씀
프롬프트 하나를 쓰는 사람에게 실제로 달라지는 게 뭔지 의문임
글쓴이에게는 9월 이후 달라진 게 없음

그런데도 타임라인은 축하 분위기임
“모든 것이 달라진다”는 말은 9월 Opus 5.5 때도, 그 전 Astra 때도 나왔음
몇 주 뒤면 다음 모델을 두고 또 같은 말이 나올 것임

이 경쟁에 지쳤음
몇 주마다 새로운 숫자와 새로운 과열 반응이 나오지만, 그 때문에 달라진 행동 하나도 꼽을 수 없음

items.title: Google touts AI breakthrough, path to "unhackable" software
items.summary:
To test the system, researchers reintroduced two previously fixed bugs into Signal's code. In both cases, the AI-powered framework generated mathematical proofs showing that the altered software was insecure.

The intrigue: But Chaudhuri told Axios that the AI lab's tools were able to accomplish this feat in just four weeks — compared to the years it would've likely taken humans alone. [...] Driving the news:Google DeepMind said Tuesday it used AI agents powered by its Gemini 4 Carbon model to mathematically verify that the code underpinning Signal's encryption is secure.

   The agents generated more than 3 million lines of mathematical proofs in the process, allowing researchers to verify the software at a level of detail previously considered impractical. [...] Google DeepMind researchers have used AI to mathematically prove that the encryption code protecting billions of private messages works as intended.

Why it matters: The research breakthrough could eventually help defenders build better software. "You can finally get to this world of unhackable software," said Swarat Chaudhuri, a research scientist at Google DeepMind.

items.title: New model helps robots learn tasks faster with less human programming
items.summary:
Called agentic robotics, the approach allows teams of AI agents to generate robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments, identify failures, and revise their code before deploying it on physical machines.

The technology could address two longstanding challenges in robotics: the extensive engineering required to program robot behaviors and the large volumes of real-world data needed to train robots through imitation learning. [...] Agentic robotics seeks to combine the advantages of these methods while reducing their limitations. The approach uses a framework called Graph-as-Policy, which divides complex robotic tasks into smaller, reusable skills. These include identifying objects, planning grasps, and moving robotic grippers without colliding with surrounding objects. [...] UC Berkeley researchers have developed an AI-driven approach that could significantly accelerate how robots are programmed and trained for real-world tasks. Called agentic robotics, the approach uses teams of AI agents to generate robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments, and refine their performance.

The method could reduce the need for extensive training data and manual engineering, two major challenges that have slowed the development of capable robots.

With adaptive development, the parts technology, cost control, and mass production experience accumulated by the auto industry can migrate to the robotics sector. Embodied robots have a better chance of proving their value in flexible assembly, multi-task switching, and complex operations.

Simple work is already handled well by traditional automation; complex work is where embodied robots are still proving themselves. [...] Yang mentioned in the interview that beyond simply substituting human labor, data generated by robot operations can be used to improve capacity planning, quality tracking, and equipment prediction—thereby helping factories boost efficiency and cut costs.

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
